original:
Do as thou hast said. 2 Samuel 7:25. David praying back to God the very promise God just made him. There is a confidence in it I have spent most of my life not quite reaching. I have prayed too politely, Father. I have edited Your promises down to what seemed reasonable for me to ask. At this age I am tired of editing. Do as You have said. About the home You have prepared. About the saints who shall reign with Him. About the new heavens and the new earth where there will be no more crying nor pain. About the kindness toward the wandering one of mine that I still trust You for, on the strength of nothing but what You have already promised. I will not invent promises You did not make, because that is its own old sin and I am not interested in adding to it. I will only stop softening the ones You did make. Let the small prayers in this house this morning have a bit of David's nerve in them. Not because I have grown bolder. Because You have been so reliable for so long that pretending otherwise has become exhausting.

Amen.
rewritten:
Father, David prayed Your promise back to You: "Do as You have said." I have spent many years praying politely, sometimes editing Your promises down to what seemed reasonable to ask.

I do not want to invent promises You never made. Keep me from that. But I also do not want to soften the promises You did make. Do as You have said about the home You have prepared. Do as You have said about resurrection, mercy, and the day when crying and pain will be finished. Do as You have said for the wandering one I still bring to You.

Give the prayers in this house a little of David's nerve today. Not because I have become impressive, but because You have been faithful for so long that pretending otherwise has become exhausting.

Amen.
